title: Chunk Overlap Tuning
summary: Tune shared text between neighboring chunks to preserve boundary evidence without filling retrieval results with duplicates.
overview: Chunk overlap repeats some source content across adjacent retrieval units so facts spanning a boundary remain recoverable. It is a hedge against imperfect segmentation, especially when paragraphs, definitions, or procedure steps extend across a fixed-size cut. Overlap is not a universal percentage: the right amount depends on document structure, tokenizer behavior, and retrieval tasks.

More overlap increases embedding and storage work and can make top results redundant. It may also bias ranking toward repeated text or inflate apparent evidence counts. Evaluate overlap jointly with chunk size, structural boundaries, parent expansion, and deduplication rather than optimizing it in isolation.

production.poc: A prototype tests several chunk-size and overlap pairs against questions whose answers cross boundaries.
production.production: Production uses source offsets, stable chunk IDs, and duplicate-aware evaluation to distinguish real coverage from repeated passages.
production.scale: At scale, tune by document family, estimate re-indexing costs, and track how overlap affects context tokens and retrieval diversity.

components.name: Structure-aware splitter
components.role: Prefers paragraphs, headings, and table boundaries where available.

components.role: Defines token or structural overlap by document class.

components.name: Chunk lineage store
components.role: Preserves document revision and exact source ranges.

flow.title: Inspect source structure
flow.description: Identify the units that carry meaning, including headings, tables, and list conditions.

flow.title: Select candidate settings
flow.description: Choose several chunk and overlap configurations within embedding limits.

flow.title: Generate versioned chunks
flow.description: Record source offsets and revision identity for every chunk.

flow.title: Evaluate boundary recall
flow.description: Test questions requiring information on both sides of a proposed cut.

flow.title: Measure redundancy
flow.description: Count repeated source ranges in retrieved results and assembled context.

flow.title: Deploy by document class
flow.description: Choose the smallest evaluated overlap that preserves needed evidence and retain a migration plan.

useCase.title: Retrieving specification conditions
useCase.situation: A project assistant searches technical specifications containing requirements followed by exceptions on the next paragraph.
useCase.problem: Fixed chunk boundaries separate a material requirement from its installation condition.
useCase.requirement: Retrieve both parts while keeping duplicate specification text out of the answer context.
useCase.architecture: A structure-aware splitter uses limited overlap and source-range deduplication.
runtime: A query matches the requirement near a boundary.
The neighboring condition is present through overlap, and the context assembler merges shared ranges.
useCase.failure: If a large table exceeds chunk limits, a dedicated table strategy preserves headers instead of relying on overlap alone.
useCase.impact: Measure boundary-question accuracy, duplicated context ratio, and total index size; overlap should solve a demonstrated segmentation failure.

tradeoffs.cost: Require reliable parsing of varied formats.

failures.detection: Most hits cover the same source range.
failures.recovery: Deduplicate by offsets and increase evidence diversity.

failures.detection: Values retrieve without their column meanings.
failures.recovery: Use table-aware chunking with repeated validated headers.

mistakes.fix: Version the chunking policy and rebuild consistently.

whenToUse: Use when important facts cross chunk boundaries.
Use for imperfectly structured long documents.
whenNotToUse: Avoid large overlap for self-contained short records.
Do not expect overlap to repair broken document extraction.
Avoid optimizing overlap independently of chunk size.
